candidate_relations.reason: HFpEF-range findings (extreme BNP, LVH) are cardiac consequences of severe hypertension, not mixed LCH/ECD with renovascular hypertension.
Giant cell arteritis is a different vasculitis and does not capture mixed LCH/ECD.
Fibromuscular dysplasia is an incompatible cause of ostial renal and mesenteric stenoses versus histiocytosis-related perivascular disease.
Liddle syndrome is a different genetic hypertension and does not explain histiocytosis or arterial stenoses.
Mixed LCH and ECD with renovascular hypertension matches the reference and the prior LCH history plus ostial renal-artery disease and severe hypertension.
Loeys-Dietz syndrome is a different genetic arteriopathy, not mixed histiocytosis.
Renovascular hypertension due to FMD has the hypertension component but an incompatible FMD etiology versus mixed LCH/ECD.
Langerhans cell histiocytosis with renovascular hypertension is a compatible component but omits required Erdheim-Chester disease in the mixed diagnosis.
Heart failure is a downstream cardiac manifestation, not the mixed histiocytosis diagnosis.
Erdheim-Chester disease is a required component but omits mixed LCH and renovascular hypertension.
Marfan syndrome is a different connective-tissue arteriopathy.
Histiocytic disorders are the parent family and lack mixed LCH/ECD plus renovascular hypertension.
Systemic vasculitis is a competing large-vessel stenosis explanation, not mixed LCH/ECD.
Pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1 is a different salt-wasting disorder, not this hypertensive histiocytosis.
Atherosclerotic disease is an incompatible etiology for ostial renal/celiac/SMA stenoses in this histiocytosis context.
Takayasu arteritis with renal-artery stenosis is a related steno-occlusive vasculitis with incompatible etiology versus mixed LCH/ECD.
Hypertension is present but omits mixed LCH/ECD and the renovascular mechanism.
Atherosclerotic renal-artery stenosis conflicts with histiocytosis-related ostial disease and omits mixed LCH/ECD.
Atherosclerosis is a different arterial disease, not mixed LCH/ECD.
Pheochromocytoma is a different endocrine hypertension and no adrenal mass is described.
